questions.question: The minerals lying closest to the top of the earth's surface can be excavated by the _______ process.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quarrying.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Minerals that lie near the surface are simply dug out, by the process known as **Quarrying.**
 
• A quarry is a type of open pit mine in which dimension stone, rock, construction aggregate, sand, gravel, or slate is excavated from the underground

questions.question: What does the letter 'V' stand for in HVJ pipeline, which is India's first inter-state inland natural gas pipeline?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijaipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) pipeline** is **India's first cross-state gas pipeline.**
 
• The project began in 1986, with the **formation of GAIL (India)** Limited, with the goal of supplying gas to fertiliser facilities in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The project's first phase, consisting of a 1,750-kilometer non-branched grid, was completed in 1987.
 
• The addition of new branches to supply gas for industrial and home usage across Rajasthan, Haryana, and the National Capital Territory, brings the overall grid length to 3,474 kilometers.
 
• **Indraprastha Gas Limited**, a newly formed company, gained control of the Delhi branch of the pipeline in 1998 in order to construct a citywide gas system.
 
• It has branches in Rajasthan's Kota, Uttar Pradesh's Shahajahanpur, Babrala, and other cities. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **GAIL Limited**, based in GAIL Bhawan in New Delhi, India, is a government-owned natural gas explorer and producer responsible for natural gas processing and distribution in India.
 
• It is owned by the Indian government's Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

questions.question: Which of the following is a low grade brown coal that is soft with high moisture content?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lignite.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Lignite**

 
 
• Lignite coal, often known as **brown coal**, is the **lowest grade of coal **with the** lowest carbon content.**
 
• It is mostly employed in **energy generation** due to its **low heating value** and **high moisture content.**
 
 
 
• **​Bituminous**
 
 
• Bituminous coal is a coal that falls in between sub-bituminous and anthracite in terms of rank.
 
• Bituminous coal has a** high heating value (Btu) **and is utilized in the United States for** electricity generation and steel production**.
 
• When first encountering bituminous coal, it appears** blocky and shiny, and smooth**, but closer inspection reveals **thin, alternating, shiny, and dull layers.**
 
 
 
• ​** Anthracite**
 
 
• The** highest rank** of coal.
 
• It is a** hard, brittle, black glossy coal** with a **high percentage of fixed carbon** and a **low percentage of volatile matter**, sometimes referred to as** hard coal.**
 
 
 
• **​Peat**
 
 
• ​Peat is a **precursor** of coal.
 
• Peat is a** soft, organic substance** made up of **partially decomposed plant and mineral materials**.
 
• Peat undergoes physical and chemical changes (coalification) to become coal when it is exposed to** high pressure and heat.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fossil fuel ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Biomass.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Biomass is a renewable energy source** that comes** from plants and animals.**
 
• **Biomass contains** stored** chemical energy from the sun.**
 
• **Plants** produce** biomass through photosynthesis.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biomass sources** for energy include:-

 
 
• **Wood and wood processing wastes** — firewood, wood pellets, and wood chips, lumber and furniture mill sawdust, and waste, etc.
 
• **Agricultural crops and waste materials** — corn, soybeans, sugar cane, switchgrass, woody plants, and algae, and crop and food processing residues.
 
• **Biogenic materials in municipal solid waste** — paper, cotton, and wool products, and food, yard, and wood wastes.
 
• **Animal manure and human sewage.**
 
 
 
• **Fossil fuel** is a fuel **formed by natural processes**.
 
• It is **natural fuel **such as** coal, Petroleum products, and Natural gas,** that was **formed millions of years ago **from **dead animals or plants in the ground.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Burning either fossil fuels or biomass releases carbon dioxide (CO₂), a greenhouse gas. **
 
• India's** Rank in Global Energy Transition Index** -** 74.**
 
• **Bitumen **is a low-grade of crude oil which is composed of complex, heavy hydrocarbons. 
 
• **Asphalt**, a black or brown **petroleum-like material **that has a consistency varying from viscous liquid to glassy solid.

questions.question: Which of the following is known as alkaline earth metal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnesium**__.

__
 
• **Magnesium** is known as **alkaline earth metal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The **alkaline earth metals** are named after the **alkaline earth **whose old-fashioned names were** beryllia, magnesia, lime, strontia,** and** baryta,** after their **oxides**. When mixed with** water,** these **oxides are simple** (alkaline).
 
• The elements of Group 2 of the periodic table are alkaline earth metals.
 
• **Beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium,** and** radium** are the elements in **Group 2**.
 
 
• For** two reasons**, these elements are referred to as **Alkaline Earth metals.** Their oxides remain in the **crust **of the **earth **and are** very heat-stable.**
 
 
 
• **In group 1 **of th**e periodic table**, **alkali metals **are the** elements**.
 
 
• The key distinction between **alkaline** and **alkali** is that there is **one valence electron** in **alkali metals**, while **two valence electrons** are in **alkaline earth metals.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 **Metal**
 **Details**
 
 

 **Copper**
 
 
 
• Copper is a chemical element with the symbol Cu and atomic number 29.
 
• Atomic mass: 63.546 u
 
• Melting point: 1,085 °C. 
 
 
 
 

 **Platinum**
 
 
 
• Platinum is a chemical element with the symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
 
• Atomic mass: 195.084 u
 
• Melting point: 1,768 °C
 
 
 
 

 **Cobalt**
 
 
 
• Cobalt is a chemical element with the symbol Co and atomic number 27.
 
• Atomic mass: 58.933195 u
 
• Melting point: 1768 K 
 
 
 
 

 **Magnesium**
 
 
 
• Magnesium is a chemical element with the symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
 
• Atomic mass: 24.305 u
 
• Melting point: 650 °C

questions.question: Tummalapalle, believed to have one of the largest uranium reserves in the world, is situated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Andhra Pradesh**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• The **Tummalapalle Mine** is a uranium mine located in **Kadapa** in the Indian state of **Andhra Pradesh,** in the **village of Tumalapalli.**
 
• Results from research conducted by **India's Atomic Energy Commission** in 2011 have led analysts to conclude that this mine may have one of the world's largest uranium reserves. 
 
• On 19 July 2011, **Dr. S. Banerjee**, Secretary of the Department of Atomic Energy, who was also Chairman of the Indian Atomic Energy Commission, confirmed reserves of **49,000** **tonnes** and suggested that it could be three times larger to make Tummalapalle the largest uranium deposit mine in the world.
 
• In 2014, the estimates were subsequently raised to **85,000 tonnes.**
 
• Recent findings allegedly show that the reserves are as deep as **1,000 meters.**
 
• This finding has significantly increased India's ability to generate energy from nuclear power plants.
 
• India produced about **3.13 percent** of its energy from nuclear plants as of 2018.
 
• These results indicate that this output can be increased to more than **30 percent** by 2050, which is essential if India hopes to reduce its carbon emissions, pollution, and use.
 
• Not only will this domestic uranium discovery improve India's nuclear energy ambitions, but it will also help cut costs by moving from costly electricity sources like coal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Facts** about Andhra Pradesh:

 
 
• **Legislative Capital:** Amaravati
 
• **Population**: 4.94 crores (2011)
 
• **Chief minister:** N. Chandrababu Naidu
 
• **Governor**: Shri Justice Nazeer
 
• **Founded**: 1 November 1956

questions.question: Koteshwar Hydroelectric Power Project is located on the river ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhagirathi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Koteshwar Dam__

 __
 
• It is a gravity dam on the Bhagirathi River, located 22 km from the Tehri Dam in Tehri District, Uttarakhand.
 
• The dam is part of the Tehri Hydropower Complex and serves to regulate the Tehri Dam's tailrace for irrigation and create the lower reservoir of the Tehri Pumped Storage Power Station.
 
 
 
• Bhagirathi__​
 __
 
• The Bhagirathi river is a Himalayan river that flows in Uttarakhand State.
 
• It is one of the two headstreams of the pious Ganga river.
 
• It originates from Gaumukh Glacier and flows about 193 km before merging with Alaknanda to form River Ganga at Devprayag.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gomati**__

 __
 
• The Gomti river is a Monsoon and Groundwater fed river.
 
• That originated from Gomat Taal (earlier known as Fulhaar jheel) near Madho Tanda, Pilibhit district of Uttar Pradesh state.
 
• It is a tributary of the Ganges river. 
 
• Its length extends 960 km through Uttar Pradesh and meets the Ganges river near Saidpur, and Kaithi 27 km from Varanasi district of Uttar Pradesh state.
 
 
 
• ​**Koshi**__
 __
 
• The Kosi is a 720 km long transboundary river which flows through Nepal, Tibet and India. 
 
• It drains the northern slopes of Tibet and the southern slopes of Nepal.
 
• It is also known as Saptakoshi due to its seven upper tributaries, namely, the **Indrawati, the Sun Koshi, the Tama Koshi, the Likhu, the Dudh Koshi, the Arun and the Tamor**. 
 
 
 
• **Damodar**__
 
• The source of the Damodar river is Chota Nagpur Plateau (Palamau hills in Jharkhand) and the mouth is Hooghly River, Rupnarayan River.
 
• The river bifurcates into two channels at Beguahana.
 
 
• The main flow passes through the Mundeswari channel and discharges into Rupnarayan.
 
• The other one Amta channel carries discharge during high floods and outfalls into the Hooghly.
 
 
 
• **The Damodar River in India has four main dams:**

 Tilaiya: Located on the Barakar River

 Maithon: Located on the Barakar River

 Panchet: Located on the Damodar River

 Konar: Located on the Konar River

questions.question: Which is the highest quality hard coal of the below?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anthracite.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Anthracite** is the highest quality of hard coal.

 
 
• Anthracite is the most highly metamorphosed form of coal.
 
• It contains around 86% fixed carbon and 14% volatile matter.
 
• Anthracite considered the least plentiful form of coal.
 
 
 
• **Coal** is considered the most abundantly available fossil fuel.
 
 
• It provides a substantial part of the nation’s energy needs.
 
• Coal is formed due to the compression of plant material over a long period of time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lignite** is low-grade brown coal.

 
 
• Lignite is soft with high moisture content.
 
• The principal lignite reserves are in Neyveli in Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **Bituminous coal **is the coal that has been buried deep and subjected to increased temperatures.
 
 
• Bituminous coal is the most popular coal in commercial use.
 
 
 
• Decaying plants in swamps produce **peat coal.**
 
 
• Peat has low carbon and high moisture content and low heating capacity.

questions.question: The mineral Carnotite is an important source of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__U__**__**ranium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **K₂(UO₂)₂(VO₄)₂.3H₂O** is the chemical formula for **carnotite, a potassium uranium vanadate radioactive mineral.**
 
• Carnotite is made up of** roughly 53% uranium, 13% vanadium, **and trace quantities of radium.
 
• It was generated by alteration of primary uranium-vanadium minerals and is of secondary origin.
 
• It's commonly found in sandstone with tyuyamunite, either diffused or as small pure masses, especially around fossil wood.
 
• Carnotite was mined for vanadium and radium from 1911 to 1923 and produced the majority of uranium output from secondary deposits. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uranium** is a silvery-white metallic chemical element with **atomic number 92 **in the periodic table.
 
• The chemical symbol for it is **U.**
 
• **Copper** is a chemical element with the** atomic number 29** and the symbol **Cu.**
 
• **Zinc** is a chemical element with the** atomic number 30** and the symbol **Zn**.
 
• At room temperature, zinc is a slightly brittle metal with a silvery-greyish look when oxidation is removed.
 
• The chemical element** iron** has the symbol **Fe** and the **atomic number 26. **

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest bauxite producing state in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Odisha__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Odisha **is the **largest bauxite-producing state in India.**
 
• **Panchpatmali deposits** in the **Koraput district** are the **most valuable bauxite deposits in the state.**
 
• Bauxite deposits are formed by the decomposition of a wide variety of rocks rich in **aluminium silicates.**
 
• **India’s bauxite deposits** are mainly found in the **Amarkantak plateau**, **Maikal hills** and the plateau region of **Bilaspur-Katni**.
 
• Though several ores contain aluminium, it is from bauxite, a clay-like substance that alumina and later aluminium is obtained. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chief Minister of Odisha - Mohan Charan Majhi

questions.question: Which of the following states has the highest coal reserve?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Jharkhand.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jharkhand has the largest reserves of coal in India followed by Odisha and Chhattisgarh**. 
 
• **The Coal Resources of India:**
 
 
• It is mainly available in older Gondwana Formations of peninsular India and younger Tertiary formations of the north-eastern region.
 
• About 80 per cent of the coal deposits in India are of the bituminous type and are of non-coking grade.
 
• The most important Gondwana coal fields of India are located in Damodar Valley.
 
• They lie in the Jharkhand-Bengal coal belt and the important coalfields in this region are Raniganj, Jharia, Bokaro, Giridih, and Karanpura.

 Jharia is the largest coalfield followed by Raniganj.
 
• The other river valleys associated with coal are the Godavari, Mahanadi, and Sone.
 
• The most **important coal-mining centre** is Singrauli in Madhya Pradesh (part of Singrauli coalfield lies in Uttar Pradesh), Korba in Chhattisgarh, Talcher, and Rampur in Odisha, Chanda-Wardha, Kamptee, and Bander in Maharashtra, and Singareni in Telangana and Pandur in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **Tertiary coals **occur in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, and Nagaland. It is extracted from Darangiri, Cherrapunji, Mewlong, and Langrin (Meghalaya); Makum, Jaipur, and Nazira in upper Assam, Namchik - Namphuk (Arunachal Pradesh), and Kalakot (Jammu and Kashmir).
 
• The lignite reserves stand at a level of around 36 billion tons, of which 90 % occur in the southern State of Tamil Nadu.
